Zhang Yichao was from Shazhou. The Zhang family had served as generals of Shazhou for generations, living in prosperity. Zhang Yichao ate fine food and wore silk, yet he often heard the cries of slaves outside his window. Knowing they shared the same roots, he felt deep sorrow. 
By the Dahe era, Zhang Yichao was over thirty, still practicing Buddhism in the temple. He was often mocked for failing to fulfill any of his grand aspirations from years before. At such times, his master, Facheng, would have him recite scriptures aloud, urging him to calm his mind and wait for the right moment. 
In the second year of Dazhong, internal strife erupted in Shazhou. Yichao raised his banner, riding the momentum of a single spark that started a prairie fire, recapturing the lands of Hexi and sending news of victory back to Tang. Henceforth, people did not call him Yichao, but Great General Zhang. The Guiyi Army's flags fluttered boldly in Hexi, and none dared challenge them.

Hong never imagined he would one day journey so far.
The arduous path north to Hutuo exposed him to refugees everywhere, skirmishes with deserters, and threats from bandits.
Along the way, his appearance grew disheveled, his Qing robe soaked, his belongings lost,
yet the memento plaque gifted by his junior brothers remained safely tucked by his side.

But the thousand-mile trek inadvertently chipped a corner of the jade plaque.
Annoyed by his carelessness, he resolved to repair it when time allowed.
Straightening his attire, he pressed onward,
toward another fractured corner amidst the war-torn lands beyond the mountains.
That realm, too, awaited his mending.
